stages.name: Trade cycle
stages.title: Trade cycle
stages.sub: Understand how actual growth moves around the trend over time to form the trade cycle.

steps.q: Over 20 years, a country's actual growth rate is sometimes above its long-term trend rate and sometimes below it, never sitting still on the trend. What does this tell you about actual growth compared to the trend?
steps.right: It moves up and down around the trend
steps.wrong: It always stays exactly on the trend
steps.hint: Think about whether real-world growth ever sits perfectly still on the average.

steps.q: When actual growth rises well above trend, output and spending surge; when it falls well below trend, they shrink. What do these two extremes look like on the cycle?
steps.right: A high point and a low point
steps.wrong: A permanent rise and a fall
steps.hint: Think of the two extreme points growth can reach, one high and one low.

steps.q: After a slump, does the economy simply stay there forever, or does it eventually move through recovery back towards another boom, then downturn again?
steps.right: It moves through the same stages again and again
steps.wrong: It stays in that one stage permanently
steps.hint: Look back over many decades of data: does the same sequence of ups and downs keep happening?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 3 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: If you plotted a country's actual growth rate on a graph over many decades, would you expect to see a repeating wave-like pattern of booms and slumps around the trend, or a flat straight line?
steps.hint: Think about whether growth ever settles down and stops changing.
